requirement_text.REQ-064: Execute Decision 0006's D2: drop tenant_id from the ten schema-isolated business tables. Approved design (PASS on first gate pass, all 4 flagged corrections independently re-verified): lib/letflow/design/req064-drop-tenant-id.md.

task.description:
Implement lib/letflow/design/req064-drop-tenant-id.md in full. Read the design doc in full before writing any code -- it went through one clean gate pass with 4 specific corrections to the original requirement text independently re-verified, so implement exactly what it specifies, not the requirement text's now-superseded module names/call-site counts.

Key points from the design (do not deviate without flagging why in your handoff):
- Letflow.Engine.TokenRecord (not Engine.Token, which is REQ-044's separate in-memory struct) owns the tokens table's tenant_id field.
- 14 tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call sites across definitions.ex/event_store.ex/promotion_review_store.ex, each with its own per-site decision in the design -- two definitions.ex sites (activate/2, rollback_definition_version/4) are explicitly LEFT UNCHANGED because tenant_id there feeds a real service-scope/permission-checker consumer, not column-stamping. Do not touch those two.
- A third users index (index(:users, [:tenant_id, :status, :inserted_at])) gets dropped with no replacement per the design's §7.2 open-question resolution (confirmed safe by the design gate -- no query filters on status+inserted_at within a tenant schema).
- Two composite indexes simplify with the idempotency contract restated in the new migration's header (promotion_reviews, promotion_assertion_runs).
- Moduledoc updates needed on more modules than the original requirement text named: Engine.Task, Engine.TokenRecord, Identity.User, Identity.Group, and all three EventStore schema modules (Event, ArchivedEvent, InstanceProjection) -- each currently has tenant_id-describing prose that must be corrected, not left stale.
- Do NOT delete TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 itself -- only its now-unneeded stamping call sites.
- Do NOT touch the four D3 tables (tenant_schemas, solution_pack_installs, solution_pack_artefact_bases, pack_update_resolutions) -- tenant_id there is a real FK, out of scope.

Self-review checklist (WF-02 §2a, plus this run's own specifics):
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors must exit 0
- mix ecto.migrate applies cleanly against a real/Docker Postgres for the new drop-tenant_id migration(s), applied against at least one real provisioned tenant schema
- Every one of the 10 schema modules' tenant_id field/cast/validate_required entries removed per the design's confirmed module list (TokenRecord, not Token)
- The two definitions.ex call sites left unchanged compile correctly and still function (their consumers -- run_service_scope_validator/3, the permission_checker -- are untouched)
- Moduledoc text updated on every module the design names, not just the two the original requirement text named
- No SQL string interpolation of tenant/user input (INV-7) in the new migration
acceptance_criteria: All migrations apply cleanly against a fresh DB via mix ecto.migrate
None of the ten confirmed tables has a tenant_id column after migration, verified against information_schema.columns in a real provisioned tenant schema
The four D3 tables retain tenant_id with their FK intact, untouched
The two composite indexes are simplified per the design, with the idempotency contract preserved
The two definitions.ex call sites (activate/2, rollback_definition_version/4) are unchanged and still compile/function
Every moduledoc the design names is updated, not left describing a removed field

result.summary: Implemented lib/letflow/design/req064-drop-tenant-id.md in full: ten new tenant-scoped migrations drop tenant_id from events, events_archive, instance_projections, process_definitions, tokens (Letflow.Engine.TokenRecord, per the design's corrected module list), tasks, promotion_reviews, promotion_assertion_runs, users, groups; both composite indexes (uq_promotion_review_active_digest, uq_promotion_assertion_runs_idempotency) simplified per the design's exact before/after with idempotency contract restated in each migration header; the third users index (users_tenant_id_status_inserted_at_index) dropped with no replacement per the design's §7 resolution; ten schema modules' field/cast/validate_required entries removed; moduledocs updated on Engine.Task, Engine.TokenRecord, Identity.User, Identity.Group, and all three EventStore schema modules. All 14 tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call sites in definitions.ex/event_store.ex/promotion_review_store.ex handled per the design's per-site table -- the two definitions.ex sites (activate/2 line 506, rollback_definition_version/4 line 687) left unchanged as specified, feeding run_service_scope_validator/permission_checker respectively. tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 itself untouched; the four D3 tables (tenant_schemas, solution_pack_installs, solution_pack_artefact_bases, pack_update_resolutions) untouched, verified by direct information_schema query against a real provisioned tenant schema. During implementation, found and fixed three real breaks the design's artifacts_in list did not cover, all direct, mandatory consequences of the same column drops: (1) lib/letflow/definitions.ex's run_rollback_transaction/4 and supersede_matching_review/4 (both in rollback_definition_version/4's call graph, downstream of the 'unchanged' line-687 site) queried d.tenant_id/r.tenant_id directly on process_definitions/promotion_reviews -- fixed to rely on prefix-scoping alone, tenant_id parameters dropped from both plus finish_rollback/8 and do_rollback/6 (the latter's param prefixed _tenant_id rather than removed, to keep rollback_definition_version/4's own call site to do_rollback/6 exactly as the design specified); (2) lib/letflow/identity.ex's get_by_external_identity/3 queried Repo.get_by(User, tenant_id: ...) directly -- fixed to rely on prefix-scoping alone; (3) lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex's promote_definition/3 read target_tenant_id from review.tenant_id (a field now gone from PromotionReview) and both write_target_definition/5 and deprecate_previous_active/3 stamped/queried process_definitions.tenant_id directly -- fixed to read target_tenant_id from plan["target_tenant_id"] (already present in serialised_plan via PromotionPlan.t(), not a new/less-trusted source) and drop the tenant_id filter from the deprecate query. Also fixed lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex's copy_groups/2, copy_users/2, copy_tenant_roles/2 (REQ-063's legacy-to-per-tenant cutover copy, still live/tested): these read FROM the legacy public.groups/public.users tables via Letflow.Identity.Group/User Ecto queries filtering on g.tenant_id/u.tenant_id -- since those schema modules just lost the field, the query macro would no longer compile; switched to fragment/2 raw-column references since the SOURCE side of this one-time copy still legitimately queries the about-to-be-dropped legacy public columns (the destination per-tenant insert side already drops tenant_id automatically via Ecto.Changeset.change/1 on the now-field-less struct, no code change needed there). All three fixes flagged here for REVIEWER since they go beyond artifacts_in but were required for mix compile --warnings-as-errors to stay clean and for the affected functions to still work at runtime -- none is a re-decision of anything in Decision 0006/0003, all are mechanical consequences of the same column drops the design specifies.
issues: Three real breaks found beyond the design's artifacts_in list, all fixed (see summary): lib/letflow/definitions.ex (run_rollback_transaction/4, supersede_matching_review/4, finish_rollback/8, do_rollback/6 tenant_id-column-query cleanup downstream of rollback_definition_version/4), lib/letflow/identity.ex (get_by_external_identity/3), lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex (promote_definition/3, write_target_definition/5, deprecate_previous_active/3 -- review.tenant_id source removed, replaced with plan["target_tenant_id"]), and lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex (copy_groups/2, copy_users/2, copy_tenant_roles/2 -- switched to fragment/2 for the legacy-public-table read side). REVIEWER should re-confirm these are correct scope, not re-decisions of anything settled by Decision 0006/0003 -- they are mechanical consequences of the column drops, not new design choices.

mix test (informational, not this handoff's gate): confirmed 32 test files reference tenant_id, ~20 constructing struct literals against the ten changed schema modules; test/letflow/event_store/schemas_test.exs fails to compile at %InstanceProjection{tenant_id: ...} as the first example hit. This is expected fallout from the schema change and is TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER's downstream job per WF-02, not fixed here -- flagging so REVIEWER and the next steps aren't surprised by red CI before TEST-DESIGNER updates the affected specs.
